claims.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Penguins.

claims.head: Like for like: Hertl against Kindel
claims.call: The Golden Knights’ L3 (Hertl, Lavoie and Connelly) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Penguins’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Hertl’s line (Hertl, Lavoie and Connelly) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Penguins’ third line is Robertson, Kuzmenko and Kindel.

claims.head: Second night of a back-to-back for the Penguins
claims.body: The Penguins played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Golden Knights to control more of the play than they usually do.

notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang.
Egor Chinakhov is out (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Ville Koivunen has taken his spot beside Evgeni Malkin and Tommy Novak.
Spencer Stastney joined from EDM on Oct 7 and has played beside Kris Letang.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights should be favored
VGK.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Pittsburgh is on the second night of a back-to-back. It’s on the Penguins to make it a game, and they can if they get good looks.

PIT.head: A steep climb for the Penguins
PIT.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Pittsburgh is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Penguins can still win it if they get good looks, but a lot has to go their way.

story.head: Korczak returns to Vegas
paras: The Golden Knights have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Calgary. The Penguins are 3-4-1.

It’s strength against strength: the Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Ryan Craig likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Pens’ third line.

items.text: Kaedan Korczak faces Vegas for the first time since leaving.
The Penguins are newly without Trevor van Riemsdyk and Egor Chinakhov.
Jack Eichel is set to play his 700th NHL game.
Mark Stone is one point from passing William Karlsson for second on the Golden Knights’ all-time scoring list.
